rationale: M14 / R3 — a class's supertype may be a CALL, and the base's identifier is a GRANDCHILD of the call_expression, so findChildByType (DIRECT named children only) found nothing and every call-shaped heritage published NO edge at all: 76 clauses measured over the admitted population, 0 found. This pins the two shapes and the DISCRIMINATOR: (A) a member call `Base.extend(M)` puts the BASE in the receiver and the MIXINS in the arguments; (B) a plain call `MixinFn(Base)` puts the MIXIN in the callee and the BASE in the argument. The discriminator is the shape of the heritage's own expression, never a name. The negative half is the point: plain `extends` classes must publish extends and NOTHING else, so a rule that published the first identifier in any heritage would fail here; and a COMPUTED mixin (a call argument) must publish nothing, because it names nothing.

expectRelationships.note: a qualified base keeps its dotted spelling (JSD19), inside a call-shaped heritage too

forbidRelationships.note: the discriminator must not fire on a class that merely names a base
a COMPUTED mixin names nothing, so it publishes no mixin row
the receiver is the BASE, never a mixin
a mixin argument is never the base
in the plain-call shape the argument is the BASE, never a mixin
in the plain-call shape the callee is the MIXIN, never the base
